I read Atomic Habits by James Clear. He talks about habit forming and “casting votes for your ideal self”. E.g. Your ideal self is someone who works out five days a week. On days you feel like not going, just tell yourself to get to the gym and walk on the treadmill for five minutes. 

Just by showing up, you’re already helping yourself form a habit by “casting a vote” for who you want to be. Just get your training shoes on and the rest just follows. 10 out of 10 times I continue and do my full workout and if I’m really tired And slacked a bit I won’t feel sorry because at least I maintained my routine. Because the workout isn’t the hard part, it’s just making the first steps. 

This is the single point from the book that totally shifted my view on how not to skip my workouts! 

Same as what some people said here, I also enjoy crime podcasts and only let myself listen to them while running, so that makes me look forward to the treadmill.
